Multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^{2}\) so that \(I = \int_{2}^{3} \dfrac{x^{2}\,dx}{x^{3}(x^{3} - 1)}\), and put \(u = x^{3}\), \(du = 3x^{2}\,dx\); the limits become \(u = 8\) to \(u = 27\).
Then \(I = \dfrac{1}{3}\int_{8}^{27} \dfrac{du}{u(u - 1)} = \dfrac{1}{3}\int_{8}^{27}\left[\dfrac{1}{u - 1} - \dfrac{1}{u}\right] du = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\log\dfrac{u - 1}{u}\right]_{8}^{27}\).
\(\therefore I = \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\log\dfrac{26}{27} - \log\dfrac{7}{8}\right] = \dfrac{1}{3}\log\left(\dfrac{26 \times 8}{27 \times 7}\right) = \dfrac{1}{3}\log\left(\dfrac{208}{189}\right) \approx 0.03193\).

Since \(\sin^{2} x = (1 - \cos x)(1 + \cos x)\), the integrand reduces to \(\dfrac{1 - \cos x}{1 + \cos x} = \dfrac{2}{1 + \cos x} - 1 = \sec^{2}\dfrac{x}{2} - 1\).
Hence \(I = \left[2\tan\dfrac{x}{2} - x\right]_{0}^{\pi/2} = 2\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore I = \dfrac{4 - \pi}{2} \approx 0.4292\).

Put \(t = \sqrt{e^{x} - 1}\), so \(t^{2} = e^{x} - 1\), \(2t\,dt = e^{x}\,dx\) and \(e^{x} + 3 = t^{2} + 4\); the limits \(x = 0\) and \(x = \log 5\) give \(t = 0\) and \(t = 2\).
Then \(I = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{2t^{2}}{t^{2} + 4}\,dt = 2\int_{0}^{2}\left[1 - \dfrac{4}{t^{2} + 4}\right] dt = 2\left[t - 2\tan^{-1}\dfrac{t}{2}\right]_{0}^{2}\).
\(\therefore I = 2\left[2 - 2 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right] = 4 - \pi \approx 0.8584\).

Use the reduction (Wallis) formula \(\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^{m} x \cos^{n} x\,dx = \dfrac{(m - 1)(m - 3)\cdots \times (n - 1)(n - 3)\cdots}{(m + n)(m + n - 2)\cdots} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}\) when \(m\) and \(n\) are both even, with \(m = 6,\ n = 2\).
This gives \(I = \dfrac{5 \cdot 3 \cdot 1 \times 1}{8 \cdot 6 \cdot 4 \cdot 2} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{15}{384} \times \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\(\therefore I = \dfrac{15\pi}{768} = \dfrac{5\pi}{256} \approx 0.06136\).

Rationalise the denominator: \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x} - \sqrt{x}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{x}}{(1 + x) - x} = \sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{x}\).
Hence \(\int_{0}^{1}\left(\sqrt{1 + x} + \sqrt{x}\right) dx = \left[\dfrac{2}{3}(1 + x)^{3/2} + \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right]_{0}^{1} = \left(\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}\).
Comparing with \(\dfrac{k}{3}\) gives \(k = 4\sqrt{2} \approx 5.6569\).

Put \(u = \dfrac{1}{x}\), so \(du = -\dfrac{dx}{x^{2}}\); the limits \(x = 1\) and \(x = 2\) become \(u = 1\) and \(u = \dfrac{1}{2}\).
Then \(I = -\int_{1}^{1/2} e^{u}\,du = \int_{1/2}^{1} e^{u}\,du = \left[e^{u}\right]_{1/2}^{1} = e - \sqrt{e}\).
\(\therefore I = \sqrt{e}\left(\sqrt{e} - 1\right) \approx 1.0696\).

Observe that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{x}{\log x}\right) = \dfrac{\log x - 1}{(\log x)^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\log x} - \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^{2}}\), which is exactly the integrand.
Hence \(I = \left[\dfrac{x}{\log x}\right]_{2}^{e} = \dfrac{e}{\log e} - \dfrac{2}{\log 2} = e - \dfrac{2}{\log 2} \approx -0.16711\).
Comparing with \(a + \dfrac{b}{\log 2}\) gives \(a = e,\ b = -2\).

In \(I_{1} = \int_{e}^{e^{2}} \dfrac{dx}{\log x}\) put \(x = e^{t}\), so \(dx = e^{t}\,dt\) and \(\log x = t\); the limits \(x = e\) and \(x = e^{2}\) become \(t = 1\) and \(t = 2\).
Then \(I_{1} = \int_{1}^{2} \dfrac{e^{t}}{t}\,dt\), which is precisely \(I_{2}\).
\(\therefore I_{1} = I_{2} \approx 3.0591\).

By the property \(\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a - x)\,dx\) with \(a = 9\), \(I = \int_{0}^{9} \dfrac{\sqrt{9 - x}}{\sqrt{9 - x} + \sqrt{x}}\,dx\).
Adding this to the original gives \(2I = \int_{0}^{9} \dfrac{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{9 - x}}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{9 - x}}\,dx = \int_{0}^{9} 1\,dx = 9\).
\(\therefore I = \dfrac{9}{2} = 4.5\).

Let \(f(\theta) = \log\left(\dfrac{2 + \sin\theta}{2 - \sin\theta}\right)\); then \(f(-\theta) = \log\left(\dfrac{2 - \sin\theta}{2 + \sin\theta}\right) = -f(\theta)\), so \(f\) is an odd function.
The interval \(\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{4},\ \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]\) is symmetric about the origin, and \(\int_{-a}^{a} f(\theta)\,d\theta = 0\) for an odd \(f\).
\(\therefore\) the value of the integral is \(0\).
